entries.claim: A real teacher wrote the text-to-SQL training data
entries.evidence: Nemotron 3 Ultra on Nebius Token Factory wrote the databases, questions and SQL. Every SQL query ran in a sandbox and was kept only if it ran and returned rows. Round 1 (22 Oct): 821 training rows, and 172 exam rows on databases that are not in training (57 of them from two industries never trained on). Round 2 (23 Oct): 3,507 new rows from new databases; with round 1's rows, minus duplicates and 6 rows that shared a question or a query with the exam, 4,322 training rows. None of the 172 exam rows appears in them.

check.label: Read the generator: a query is kept only if it runs and returns rows

facts.label: Teacher spend
facts.value: $2.87 for round 1, $9.18 for round 2's new rows

entries.claim: LoRA adapters were trained on that data
entries.evidence: The published adapters were trained on a borrowed GPU: a 4-bit LoRA (r=16) on Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, 2 epochs each. Round 2, the headline adapter: 4,322 rows, 1,080 steps in about 5.2 hours, training loss 0.345 to 0.087. Round 1: 821 rows, 206 steps in 66 minutes, training loss 0.334 to 0.075. A training loss is not a quality result. On 27 Oct 2026 the round-2 recipe (the same 4,322 rows and settings) was retrained on Nebius AI Cloud, by hand, as a Serverless Job on one preemptible L40S with checkpoints in Object Storage: training loss 0.346 to 0.088, adapter SHA-256 68b9ed06d984a2ec38a32b58090c246a56ae12ba65f3277f66b5d74227ea25d5. It scored 40.7% (70 of 172) on exam 1 and 34.5% (69 of 200) on exam 2, against 39.0% and 33.0% for the original adapter: the result reproduces (the row-by-row differences are within chance); training took 28.6 minutes of GPU time (58.7 minutes wall clock across two spot interruptions); the whole Nebius effort, failed and interrupted attempts included, used 2.73 GPU-hours, about $2.16 at list prices (the Nebius bill decides).

facts.label: Nebius retraining (27 Oct 2026)
facts.value: Round 2 recipe, one preemptible L40S, Serverless Job, loss 0.346 to 0.088, by hand

facts.label: Round 2
facts.value: 4,322 rows, 1,080 steps over 2 epochs in about 5.2 hours

facts.label: Round 1
facts.value: 821 rows, 206 steps over 2 epochs in 66 minutes

entries.claim: How well the adapter does on two held-out exams
entries.evidence: Two exams of text-to-SQL questions on databases the models never saw: 172 written by the teacher and 200 on new industries written by a different model (Claude, for evaluation only, never training). An answer is right when running it returns the same rows as the stored reference query. Strict, exam 1 / exam 2: base 22 of 172 / 25 of 200, teacher 44 / 30, adapter round 1 (821 rows) 57 / 56, adapter round 2 (4,322 rows) 67 / 66. Every number is recomputed from the raw answers by one script. Round 2 beat round 1 on both exams, but the gain could partly be chance (p = 0.12 and 0.13); the adapter does not yet replace the teacher at a 95 percent precision target.

entries.claim: The student served on a Nebius Serverless Endpoint, for speed tests
entries.evidence: On 27 to 28 Oct 2026 the student was served by hand, in two short sessions, on a Nebius Serverless Endpoint: one preemptible L40S, vLLM v0.18.0, Nemotron 3 Nano 4B with two LoRA adapters loaded at runtime (the published round-2 text-to-SQL adapter and the tool-calling adapter). Cold start took about 7.2 minutes from create to ready (7.6 minutes in a second session); a restart (stop, then start) took about 7.1 minutes to the first answer, with the adapters loaded again. With 16 requests at once the median answer took 1.6 s (SQL adapter) and 1.2 s (tool-calling adapter). It measured speed only, on 30 ordinary prompts, not accuracy. It cost about $0.67 of GPU time across two sessions (the Nebius bill decides). The first restart crashed on cache files on the bucket mount; the fix was to keep them on local disk, and the second session's restart worked. The endpoint was deleted afterwards. The public live gateway is not connected to it: the teacher answers every live request.

facts.value: About 7.2 minutes from create to ready; both adapters loaded in about a second each

facts.value: About 53 minutes across two sessions, about $0.67 at list price

entries.claim: How well a tool-calling adapter does on two held-out exams
entries.evidence: On the hard exam the adapter is above the untrained model: 90.7% against 62.7%, and the 95% ranges do not overlap. It is about the same as the teacher: 90.7% against 91.3% (lower by point estimate, but the 95% ranges overlap, so the exam cannot tell them apart). On the BFCL exam the adapter is about the same as the untrained model: 80.3% against 77.3% (higher by point estimate, but the 95% ranges overlap, so the exam cannot tell them apart). It is lower than the teacher: 80.3% against 88.3% (241/300 against 265/300; the 95% ranges overlap only slightly, so part of the gap could be chance). Strict scoring. Free-text arguments are a known weak spot in the training data: the strict scorer cannot agree on free text, so tools such as create_ticket (15 training rows), search_files, send_payment and search_inbox are thin. The hard exam uses 20 tools that were never in training. The adapter was trained on a borrowed GPU, on synthetic data. The hard exam (150 questions, 20 new tools) was written by Claude Sonnet 5.5 for evaluation only and is never training data; the second exam (300 questions) is drawn from the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (Apache-2.0).
